title: An Ceann a Eisiatar ag Tástáil Uisce
intro: I stair na sean-scríbhinní, tá figiúr suimiúil ann nach dtosaíonn a scéal le míorúilt dhrámatúil ná le nochtadh toirneach, ach le triail chreidimh shimplí ach dhomhain. Sheas náisiún ag crosbhóthar, ag lorg treorach dhiaga le haghaidh ceannaireachta. An rud a tharla ná tástáil chomh cliste sin go nochtfadh sé cé na fíorchreidmhigh ina measc. An féidir leat an rúndiamhair seo a réiteach ó na leideanna a fágadh ina ndiaidh?
clues: Tháinig mé ó shliocht a raibh meas ag na daoine air, agus roghnaigh Allah mé chun críche naofa nár thuig siad.
Bhí marc idirdhealaithe ar mo chorp nach raibh ar dhaoine eile, rud a d’fhág go raibh mé i mo sheasamh ar leithligh i measc mo mhuintire.
Nuair a fógraíodh gurbh í an abhainn an tástáil, d’fhill formhór na ndaoine ar ais—ach lean mé ar aghaidh, á thiomáint ag creideamh dochloíte i ngealltanas Allah.
Tugadh ordú dom gan deoch a ól riamh ó uiscí toirmiscthe, ach níor éirigh le braon amháin imeacht ó mo bhéal—peaca a chuir isteach ar mo chroí go deo.
Chinn Allah dom bualadh le haoire óg a mbeadh clú agus cáil air lá éigin as namhaid cumhachtach a mharú.
Nuair a bhuail na hairm le chéile, ní de láimh an namhad a thit mé, ach de bharr foraithne Dé mar phionós as mo mhí-umhlaíocht ag an abhainn.

arabic: فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ بِٱلْجُنُودِ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُبْتَلِيكُم بِنَهَرٍۢ فَمَن شَرِبَ مِنْهُ فَلَيْسَ مِنِّى وَمَن لَّمْ يَطْعَمْهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّىٓ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱغْتَرَفَ غُرْفَةًۢ بِيَدِهِۦ ۚ فَشَرِبُوا۟ مِنْهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّنْهُمْ ۚ فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُۥ هُوَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ قَالُوا۟ لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا ٱلْيَوْمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ ۚ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَـٰقُوا۟ ٱللَّهِ كَم مِّن فِئَةٍۢ قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتْ فِئَةًۭ كَثِيرَةًۢ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ
verse: And when Saul went forth with the soldiers, he said, "Indeed, Allāh will be testing you with a river. So whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is indeed of me, excepting one who takes [from it] in the hollow of his hand." But they drank from it, except a [very] few of them. Then when he had crossed it along with those who believed with him, they said, "There is no power for us today against Goliath and his soldiers." But those who were certain that they would meet Allāh said, "How many a small company has overcome a large company by permission of Allāh. And Allāh is with the patient." (2:249)
